item.title: Volkswagen Plans New Audi Plant in Georgia, Handing Trump a Win
item.author: Gabrielle Coppola, Josh Wingrove and William Wilkes
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen AG will build a new factory for its premium Audi brand in Georgia and expand a facility in South Carolina, Donald Trump will announce Saturday, as the US president looks to notch a political win in the final stretch of the midterm election cycle.

item.title: Obama Issues Searing Attacks on Trump, Ramaswamy in Return to Campaign Trail
item.author: Tim Balk and Emily Davies
item.content:encoded: In his some of his most critical remarks in recent memory, the 44th president said the current administration was defined by “incompetence the likes of which we have not seen in modern times.”

item.title: Alaska Election Gambit Shows Justice Dept. Has Bowed to Trump’s Demands
item.author: Glenn Thrush, Katie Rogers and Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.content:encoded: With moves in Alaska and California, the department has stepped up interventions in the midterm elections as the president’s instrument of unmediated executive power.

item.title: In U.S. Gas Talks With Kremlin, Hidden Financing for Alaska Project Emerges
item.author: Anton Troianovski and Eric Lipton
item.content:encoded: Interviews and documents show a Russian energy giant secretly funded a U.S. firm. The deal has been discussed in talks to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Why Democrats Could Find It Hard to Win the Senate Despite Their Strong Polls
item.author: Lisa Lerer
item.content:encoded: Democrats are increasingly optimistic about the midterms. But they are being outspent by Republicans. And they are trying to compete in states that favored President Trump by large margins.

item.title: Drones on Starshield Network Are Back to Normal Speeds, Ukraine Says
item.author: Siobhán O’Grady and Liubov Sholudko
item.content:encoded: The announcement followed more than a week of unexplained problems with Starshield, the Pentagon-funded satellite network Ukraine relies on to thwart Russian attacks.

item.title: Iran in ‘Advanced Stages’ of Planning Attacks Against Americans, Officials Say
item.author: Edward Wong, Jonathan Swan and Julian E. Barnes
item.content:encoded: The U.S. government has ordered diplomats and other federal employees to leave Saudi Arabia. It is also drawing down staff at other missions in the region.

item.title: Why Is the U.S. Accusing Canada of Election Interference?
item.author: Zane Irwin
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration says Canadian officials are trying to sway the midterm elections for Democrats. Prime Minister Mark Carney says those claims have “no merit.”

item.title: Albanian Protests Turn Violent as Calls Grow for PM to Resign
item.author: Gresa Kraja
item.content:encoded: Violent clashes broke out in Tirana as protesters demanding Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation threw stones and set fires while police responded with tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets.

item.title: Bardella Reelected President of French Far-Right National Rally
item.author: James Regan
item.content:encoded: Jordan Bardella was reelected president of France’s National Rally at the far-right party’s congress in Orléans on Saturday.

item.title: Democrats’ Midterm Map Expands in Warning Sign for Republicans
item.author: Catherine Lucey
item.content:encoded: Republicans began the 2026 midterm election cycle with the Senate map as one of their biggest advantages. It hasn’t turned out that way.

item.title: Meta Unseats Musk as Tech Villain for Lula in Brazil’s Election
item.author: Augusta Saraiva
item.content:encoded: A new villain is emerging in the closing stretch of Brazil’s bitterly contested presidential election: Meta Platforms Inc.

item.title: French Protests Begin as Police Seek to Avoid Repeat of Violence
item.author: James Regan and Benoit Berthelot
item.content:encoded: Police used tear gas and a water cannon to disperse crowds in Paris after tens of thousands of people marched largely peacefully on Saturday to protest the high cost of living and insufficient school funding.

item.title: Trump Prepares for Iran Escalation After US, Israeli Elections
item.author: Magdalena Del Valle, Eric Martin and Samy Adghirni
item.content:encoded: A Middle East war that President Donald Trump said would be over in a matter of weeks now looks set to escalate as it enters its eighth month.

item.title: What This Democrat’s Surge in Texas Says About the Midterms
item.author: Lulu Garcia-Navarro
item.content:encoded: Gina Hinojosa, the Democratic nominee for governor, on her appeal to MAGA voters and her refusal to engage in the “culture wars.”

item.title: Trump Tests His Political Pull in Midterm Races
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg News White House correspondent Kate Sullivan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump is making himself a central figure in the closing days of the midterm campaign, even as some Republican candidates seek distance from him. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Sullivan discusses Trump’s rally with Florida gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds, his effort to tailor his message to individual states and his intervention in a closely watched Alaska Senate race. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Hits Back at US Proposal to Tighten Investment Limits
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: China said it “firmly opposes” a US Treasury proposal to expand the scope and increase the severity of restrictions on US investment in China, calling it discriminatory and “a typical example of an overly broad application of national security concerns.”

item.title: Has Election Spending Hit a Tipping Point?
item.content:encoded: Campaign spending is climbing as candidates, parties and super PACs pour money into the midterms, and industries including AI and crypto become more active political donors. But democratic fundraiser Blair Effron of Centerview Partners argues that some races may already have reached a saturation point where another dollar matters less than the candidate receiving it. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Vivek Ramaswamy’s Ruthless Ad in Ohio Divided Republicans
item.author: Reid J. Epstein and Campbell Robertson
item.content:encoded: The fallout from Vivek Ramaswamy’s brutal spot targeting his Democratic rival in the Ohio governor’s race showed that even in the Trump era, a political attack can be seen as going too far.

item.title: El-Sayed Needs Black Voters in Michigan. Tensions With Arab Americans Make That Harder.
item.author: Shane Goldmacher and Michael Kruse
item.content:encoded: Conflict between Michigan’s Black and Arab communities could get in the way of Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s pitch in the critical Senate race.

item.title: U.S. Pressures Mexico to Deliver a Security Win Ahead of Midterm Elections
item.author: Steve Fisher, Jack Nicas, Eric Schmitt, Maria Abi-Habib, Julian E. Barnes and Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration wants a public victory soon, as well as a potential path to U.S. military forces in Mexico.

item.title: Trump Asked Muslim Voters to Trust Him. Now Some Feel Used.
item.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs and Hamed Aleaziz
item.content:encoded: Some Muslim voters who backed Mr. Trump in 2024 say they believe he pledged his support when it was politically convenient, only to alienate and scapegoat them once he won the election.

item.title: A Fact-Check on Trump’s Election Claims
item.author: Linda Qiu and Daniel Fetherston
item.content:encoded: The president has spread false claims about ranked-choice systems, voting machines, vote counting and past results to question the integrity of elections.

item.title: Beef and Barn Dances: A Farmer Tries to Turn a Red Patch of N.C. Blue
item.author: Eduardo Medina
item.content:encoded: Democrats are largely used to losing in the mountains of western North Carolina. Jamie Ager is trying to change that.

item.title: They Were Accused of Illegal Fishing. They Ended Up in ICE Detention.
item.author: Madeleine Ngo and David Ovalle
item.content:encoded: In states like Florida, officers who hand out fishing citations and inspect produce have been deputized by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, expanding the reach of President Trump’s deportation campaign.

item.title: Ukraine Says Restrictions on Starlink Speed Have Been Lifted
item.author: Daryna Krasnolutska
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said limits on the speed of its SpaceX Starlink terminal connections had been lifted in overnight testing, a move that may ease the latest tensions between Kyiv and Washington.

item.title: France on Edge as New Protests Raise Fears of More Violence
item.author: Samy Adghirni
item.content:encoded: A new round of protests is set to hit France on Saturday, raising fears of a repeat of last weekend’s riots.

item.title: Kim Jong Un Visits China for Second Trip in Just Over a Year
item.author: Hooyeon Kim and Soo-Hyang Choi
item.content:encoded: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited the Chinese city of Dandong on Saturday, his second visit to China since September 2025 and ahead of a trip to the region by US President Donald Trump next month.

item.title: Andy Burnham Tests Labour Loyalty With Budget Built for Bond Market
item.author: Alex Wickham, Chloe Chaplain and Joe Mayes
item.content:encoded: Next week, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey must deliver what his predecessor, Rachel Reeves, couldn’t: A budget that keeps both the bond market and the governing Labour Party happy.

item.title: Serbian Vote Pits Putin-Backed Strongman Against Student Dissent
item.author: Misha Savic
item.content:encoded: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic is mimicking his ally Vladimir Putin’s plan to extend his grip on power. He wants to swap the presidency for the prime minister’s job.

item.title: Australian Lawmaker Who Lost Legs After Alleged Attack is Stable
item.author: David Stringer
item.content:encoded: An Australian lawmaker whose legs were amputated after she was struck by a car in an alleged attack outside her office in rural Victoria is in stable condition, according to hospital authorities.

item.author: Jess Bidgood

item.author: Luke Broadwater
item.content:encoded: The Justice Department has opened an inquiry into Mr. Lewandowski. President Trump has not jumped to his defense.

item.title: Gutierrez: US Has Gone Too Far With Tariffs
item.content:encoded: Carlos Gutierrez, former Commerce Secretary and CEO of Kellogg and author of Sheer Will, says trade under the Trump administration has become all-encompassing and can be used as part of geopolitical and political negotiations beyond trade itself. Gutierrez says the US has gone too far with tariffs and that easing them could help reduce inflationary pressure on American consumers. Gutierrez says the US has the infrastructure and capabilities to be a strong exporter, but should focus on high-value industries rather than making consumers pay more to bring back lower-value production. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gen. Hodges (Ret.) Says Trump Actions Help Russia's War
item.content:encoded: Gen. Ben Hodges (Ret.) says restrictions on Starlink service have dealt a significant blow to Ukraine's counter-drone capabilities and disrupted an early-warning system for incoming ballistic missiles. Hodges says it is bizarre for President Donald Trump to defend Elon Musk as a "good person" who would not do anything wrong, pointing to Trump's praise of Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong Un and comments from a Trump negotiator calling Putin a humanitarian. Hodges says he applauds first lady Melania Trump's role in helping secure relief for Ukrainian civilians, but says it represents only a small fraction of the suffering caused by Russia's war. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Appeals Court Backs Trump on Constitutionality of Detentions
item.author: Mattathias Schwartz

item.author: Alan Rappeport and Ana Swanson

item.title: Trump Advisers Give Fees Earned for Aiding Srpska to His Library
